stories.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon to paid API and AI Ultra users, previews /swarm in Antigravity

key_facts.fact: On November 10, 2026, Google made Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its strongest model, available to paying developers and enterprises via the Gemini API and Gemini for business, and to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Antigravity, the Gemini app and AI Mode in Search.
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini 4 Carbon is available via the API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises... It is also rolling out to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, the Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search.

key_facts.fact: The general rollout comes two weeks after Google released Carbon only to a select group of cybersecurity defenders.
key_facts.excerpt: Google is rolling out its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, to the general public after releasing it to a select group of “cybersecurity defenders” two weeks ago.

key_facts.fact: Introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, 2026, rising to $4 and $20 from December 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Intro (through Nov 30): $2 input · $10 output (95% off cached) From Dec 1: $4 input · $20 output

key_facts.fact: The Verge says the introductory price is around a fifth the cost of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and a quarter the cost of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2.
key_facts.excerpt: around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and a quarter the cost of Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model, which launched yesterday

key_facts.fact: Google is previewing /swarm in Antigravity, which turns one prompt into a coordinator agent, parallel workers in isolated git worktrees and adversarial verifiers that run tests and challenge diffs.
key_facts.excerpt: a coordinator that spins up specialized parallel workers in isolated git worktrees so edits never collide, and adversarial verifiers dedicated to running tests and challenging diffs

key_facts.fact: Google says Carbon ranks first on CursorBench 4.0 and Perplexity's WANDR benchmark.
key_facts.excerpt: Carbon is built to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops using more tokens (ranking #1 on CursorBench 4.0 and Perplexity’s WANDR)

key_facts.fact: Carbon thinks longer than Argon: on Artificial Analysis's index it produced 205 million tokens, almost three times the median, costing $7.76 per task at full price.
key_facts.excerpt: Running Artificial Analysis’s index, it produced 205 million tokens, almost three times the median, and cost $7.76 per task at the full price.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings, Sheets, Whiteboards and Data, taking on Microsoft and Google

key_facts.fact: At an event in San Francisco on November 10, Anthropic unveiled Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets and Claude Whiteboards, and made Claude Data (formerly Claude Dashboards) generally available.
key_facts.excerpt: At an event in San Francisco on Tuesday, Anthropic unveiled new tools... Claude Meetings, Claude Sheets, and Claude Whiteboards... Claude Data (formerly known as Claude Dashboards when it was introduced in beta in October) is now generally available to all paid plans.

key_facts.fact: Whiteboards and Sheets are in beta on all paid plans; Meetings is in beta for Team and Enterprise subscriptions.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, and Meetings are all now available in beta, with the first two available to all paid plans and Meetings available for Teams and Enterprise subscriptions.

key_facts.fact: Claude Meetings joins video calls, starting with Google Meet, takes notes and announces itself as a participant; it won't join calls with outside guests unless an admin allows it.

key_facts.fact: Claude Sheets builds spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, formatting and drop-downs from a prompt, edits cells while marking each change, and exports to .xlsx or CSV.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude can now generate spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, formatting, and drop-downs... It can edit in the cells, outlining each new edit so you can track changes... you can export your file to .xlsx or CSV

key_facts.fact: Claude Data adds certified queries, data stories and live sharing, with partners including Amplitude, Mixpanel, Omni, PostHog and Sigma.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Data adds data stories, certified queries, and live sharing... Our partners for Claude Data include Amplitude, Mixpanel, Omni, PostHog, and Sigma.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft stock fell more than 2% on the news, which came as Anthropic kicked off its IPO roadshow.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Q3 revenue jumps 50% to $10B as operating loss widens to $10.9B

key_facts.fact: OpenAI told investors its third-quarter revenue rose about 50% to $10 billion, while operating losses widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion, according to documents viewed by the Wall Street Journal.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI’s quarterly revenue rose about 50% to $10 billion in the third quarter... the company’s operating losses widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion, the WSJ report said

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved to -109% from -150% in the prior quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI told investors its adjusted operating margin improved to -109% from -150% in the prior quarter

key_facts.fact: Revenue almost tripled from a year earlier; the figures were shared on an investor call on Tuesday with President Greg Brockman, CFO Sarah Friar and product leader Thibault Sottiaux.
key_facts.excerpt: revenue increased nearly 50% from the prior quarter and almost threefold from the same period a year earlier... The financial details were shared with investors during a call on Tuesday. OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar and Thibault Sottiaux

key_facts.fact: CFO Sarah Friar said the annual run rate is roughly $50 billion, the enterprise business doubled quarter over quarter, and revenue is now split 50/50 between enterprise and consumer.
key_facts.excerpt: with an annual run rate of roughly $50 billion, CFO Sarah Friar told Deirdre Bosa on Tuesday... "Our enterprise business doubled quarter over quarter,"... OpenAI's revenue is now split 50/50 between its enterprise and consumer business.

key_facts.fact: Friar said consumer sales grew 20% quarter over quarter, subscriptions topped 100 million, and ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly active users.
key_facts.excerpt: sales improving 20% quarter over quarter and subscriptions topping 100 million users. The company has 1.2 billion weekly active users.

key_facts.fact: Rival Anthropic reported third-quarter revenue of about $17 billion, with sequential growth easing to around 47%.

stories.headline: AI 2027 authors move Superhuman AI Researcher forecast into 2027 after METR's Anthropic report

key_facts.fact: On November 10, the AI Futures Project published a timelines update in which all authors forecast that a Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) will likely arrive in 2027, absent a deliberate slowdown.
key_facts.excerpt: Now, all of us forecast that Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) will likely arrive at some point in 2027 (assuming no substantial deliberate slowdown).

key_facts.fact: The authors give a 35-65% chance that AI able to automate all white-collar work (TED-AI) arrives before 2028, and cite METR's report as the single biggest source of their update.
key_facts.excerpt: We also predict a 35-65% chance that Top-Expert-Dominating AI (TED-AI), AIs that can automate all white-collar work, will arrive before 2028... the single biggest source was the METR report.

key_facts.fact: METR's November 5 assessment found Anthropic is likely improving its models about twice as fast as between March 2024 and October 2025, with perhaps 80% of the current acceleration due to AI.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is likely improving the capabilities of their models on well-specified tasks at around twice the rate they did between March 2024 and October 2025... We guess that a majority (perhaps ≈80%) of the current (October 2026) acceleration is due to AI.

key_facts.fact: The AI Futures Project estimates METR's numbers imply a 1.7x AI-attributable speedup, which puts progress about five months ahead of the AI 2027 scenario.
key_facts.excerpt: We estimate that METR’s report implies a 1.7x AI-attributable acceleration in the pace of progress today... So by this metric, we are ~5 months ahead of schedule.

key_facts.fact: Their Monte Carlo run gives a median SAR date of July 2027, with 65% of draws reaching SAR by end-2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The Monte Carlo gives a median SAR date of July 2027, with 65% of draws reaching SAR by the end of 2027 and 84% by the end of 2028.

key_facts.fact: METR noted Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence it found most informative, which the forecasters flag as a limitation.
key_facts.excerpt: METR says that “Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence we found most informative for these conclusions”, which makes it difficult to know exactly what the 2x and 80% estimates are based on.

stories.headline: Nvidia board hires Wachtell Lipton and ex-prosecutor Joon Kim to probe Huang; shares fall 5.47%

key_facts.fact: On November 10, Nvidia's independent directors retained former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to run the investigation announced on Sunday.
key_facts.excerpt: The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: The probe covers whether company secrets or national security were compromised after Huang admitted an affair with a woman connected to Chinese intelligence; on Sunday the board said it had no reason to believe either was compromised.
key_facts.excerpt: hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang and whether company secrets or national security was compromised... Nvidia's board also said on Sunday that it has no reason to believe either national security nor Nvidia secrets were compromised.

key_facts.fact: Kim joined Wachtell only last month; in 2021 he was appointed by New York Attorney General Letitia James to investigate sexual-harassment allegations against then-Governor Andrew Cuomo.
key_facts.excerpt: Kim, a former acting attorney of the Southern District of New York, was appointed in 2021 as an independent investigator by New York Attorney General Letitia James to probe allegations of sexual harassment by former Gov. Andrew Cuomo.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has no board chair; Huang, Tench Coxe and Harvey Jones have sat on the board since 1993, and the board has a combined 161 years of service.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nvidia board has a combined 161 years of service... Huang, Tench Coxe and Harvey Jones have sat on it since 1993, according to Nvidia's proxy statement. Nvidia has a lead independent director instead of a board chair.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia shares fell 5.47% on Tuesday, November 10, after a drop of more than 4% on Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia shares sank 5.47% on Tuesday as investors continued to weigh the potential fallout from CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia closed at $168.89; Korean chipmakers still rallied the next day, with SK hynix up 5.4% and Samsung Electronics up 3.6%.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia fell to $168.89 overnight after its independent directors opened an investigation... SK hynix rose 5.4 percent to 1,277,000 won ($957.0). Samsung Electronics gained a smaller 3.6 percent to 206,000 won

stories.headline: FT: Commerce stalls Megaspeed blacklisting over four agencies' objections; scandal boosts NDAA chip curbs

key_facts.fact: The Financial Times reported on November 10 that the Pentagon and the State, Energy and Treasury departments pushed to add Singapore-based Megaspeed to the Entity List, but Commerce has delayed new additions for two months.
key_facts.excerpt: the U.S. Department of Commerce put on hold a proposal to add Singapore-based cloud provider Megaspeed to the Entity List... despite major departments, including the Departments of Defense, State and the Treasury, calling for Megaspeed to be added... delayed the process of designating new entities for sanctions over the past two months

key_facts.fact: Megaspeed's Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment with Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, and Commerce has not added any company to the Entity List in more than a year, its longest gap in 18 years.
key_facts.excerpt: Speedmatrix reportedly 'purchased at least $4.8 billion worth of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026,' per the FT... 'has not added a company to the entity list in more than a year, the longest stretch without such a listing in 18 years,'

key_facts.fact: Commerce said it needs more information on some companies, and Nvidia said it put Megaspeed on its internal block list in June 2025 and halted sales and shipments.
key_facts.excerpt: Commerce officials told other agencies they needed additional information on some companies... 'we placed the company on our internal block list in June 2025 and halted additional sales and shipments.'

key_facts.fact: Politico reported that lawmakers, aides and lobbyists say the scandal has significantly raised the chances that Congress enacts chip export limits this year in the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), and that Nvidia is now leaning on tech allies and customers to argue its case.
key_facts.excerpt: the revelation that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy has significantly raised the chances that Congress will enact chip export limits this year as part of a must-pass defense package, known as the National Defense Authorization Act... Nvidia appears to have shifted its strategy to lean on tech sector allies and major customers

key_facts.fact: Republican Rep. Jim Banks and Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren urged action on chip export controls, and a floor vote on the NDAA is seen as possible in the second week of December.
key_facts.excerpt: Republican Rep. Jim Banks and Democratic Sen. Elizabeth Warren issued a bipartisan statement urging immediate action on export controls for AI semiconductors bound for China... with a floor vote in the second week of December

stories.headline: Abu Dhabi talks end with Russia and Ukraine agreeing their largest prisoner swap; US envoys head to Moscow

key_facts.fact: US-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday, Nov. 11, after two days, with the sides agreeing a large exchange of prisoners of war.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials at U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine said Wednesday that the sides have agreed a large exchange of prisoners of war.

key_facts.fact: US envoy Jared Kushner called it 'the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners' and said numbers would be finalized the next day; Russia's Vladimir Medinsky and Ukraine's Rustem Umerov confirmed the planned exchange.
key_facts.excerpt: "One of the positives is we agreed that we're going to have the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners, which we're going to finalize the numbers tomorrow," Jared Kushner... Vladimir Medinsky, the head of the Russian delegation, and Rustem Umerov, who led Kyiv's delegation in Abu Dhabi, confirmed the planned exchange.

key_facts.fact: Kushner said the talks also made progress on how to deconflict and monitor a ceasefire, and that he and Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow on Thursday to meet Vladimir Putin, then brief Volodymyr Zelensky.
key_facts.excerpt: "We made good progress on understanding how to deconflict [..] and how to monitor the ceasefire..." Mr Kushner announced after the meetings on Wednesday that he and Mr Witkoff would travel to Moscow on Thursday to meet President Vladimir Putin

key_facts.fact: Kushner said a goal of the Moscow trip is to get Europeans added to the talks to make them multilateral; Medinsky was cool on European participation, saying it was unclear what Russia and the EU had to discuss.
key_facts.excerpt: He was cool however on the prospect of European countries joining the talks and said it was unclear what there was for Russia and the European Union to discuss, given what he said was a lack of proposals from the European side

key_facts.fact: Zelensky had said a swap could take a 1,000-for-1,000 or 1,500-for-1,500 format; the round was the first trilateral meeting since failed talks in Geneva in February.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky said a potential prisoner exchange could take place in a 1,000-for-1,000 or 1,500-for-1,500 format... The talks are the first trilateral meeting since February, when negotiations in Geneva failed to produce a breakthrough.

key_facts.fact: Russia kept attacking during the talks, striking six large electricity substations in four central Ukrainian regions, according to Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the talks, Russia struck six large electricity substations in Ukraine's four central regions, Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi said on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Hotter US October CPI cements December Fed hike bets; 2-year yield posts biggest jump since April 2025

key_facts.fact: The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October after 0.6% in September, above the 0.3% economists expected; core CPI rose 0.3% versus a 0.2% consensus.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October after advancing 0.6% in September... Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the CPI climbing 0.3%... core CPI... landed at 0.3%, higher than the 0.2% consensus.

key_facts.fact: The 2-year Treasury yield rose 18.44 basis points to 4.731%, its biggest one-day jump since the April 2025 'tariff tantrum'; the 10-year yield rose 12.55 bps to 4.988%.
key_facts.excerpt: The 2-year note yield... was last up 18.44 basis points at 4.731%. It was its biggest one-day jump since the April 2025 "tariff tantrum"... The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 12.55 bps to 4.988%.

key_facts.fact: Before the data, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a 0.3% core reading would lead him to consider a half-point hike at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Before the data landed, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in London that a core reading of 0.3% for October would prompt him to consider a half-point hike at the Fed's December 8 to 9 meeting.

key_facts.fact: Expectations for a quarter-point increase in December rose to about 90% on CME FedWatch after the release; the Fed raised rates in September for the first time in three years.
key_facts.excerpt: Expectations for a quarter-point rate increase next month rose to about 90% following the release, per the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

key_facts.fact: The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq 0.74% to 25,065.87; spot gold dropped 2.62% to $4,030.56 and Brent settled at $91.49, its lowest close since Aug. 31.
key_facts.excerpt: the S&P 500 fell 29.01 points, or 0.38%, to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 187.26 points, or 0.74%, to 25,065.87... spot gold down 2.62% at $4,030.56 an ounce... Brent futures fell $1.08, or 1.2%, to settle at $91.49 a barrel.

key_facts.fact: The October report carried no annual inflation figure because the 2025 government shutdown limited the data available for October last year.
key_facts.excerpt: October's CPI report did not include annual inflation figures because last year's government shutdown limited the data available.

stories.headline: Rubio tells G7 there is 'no need' for major combat against Iran as blockade squeezes economy

key_facts.fact: After G7 foreign ministers' meetings in Paris on Tuesday, Nov. 10, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the economic campaign against Iran is so devastating that there is no need for major combat operations.
key_facts.excerpt: "The economic campaign (against Iran) is so devastating that right now there is no need for major combat operations," the secretary of state said after a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. "That's what I told our allies here today."

key_facts.fact: Rubio rejected the idea that holding off amounts to a stalemate, saying 'never has Iran ever faced the inability to sell energy in the global market like they are today.'
key_facts.excerpt: "We don't need to conduct military strikes if we're achieving the same objective through economic means and economic pressure. That's not stalemate," Mr Rubio said. "Never has Iran ever faced the inability to sell energy in the global market like they are today."

key_facts.fact: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the conflict would not be resolved militarily or through sanctions and that Tehran's two-day proposal to reopen Hormuz remains on the table; its demands include unfreezing assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US blockade of Iranian ports.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's demands have included ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing its assets, lifting oil sanctions and ending the US blockade of its ports. "The conflict with Iran will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions," Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the IRNA news agency.

key_facts.fact: Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei said no negotiations are taking place with Washington and that Tehran is still awaiting a clear US response to its seven conditions.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei said there are currently no negotiations taking place between Tehran and Washington... Iran has insisted the US must meet seven conditions set out in a June interim agreement before the Strait of Hormuz can reopen

key_facts.fact: At a Tuesday press conference, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called the US blockade of Iranian ports 'ironclad' and said the US can maintain oversight of Iranian nuclear sites.
key_facts.excerpt: "We're able to maintain oversight and visibility of those nuclear sites. And if we saw the kind of nefarious activity that required action, we would take it," Hegseth said. Hegseth said the ongoing U.S. blockade of Iranian ports is "ironclad"

key_facts.fact: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called in Paris for moving beyond the 'no war, no peace' stalemate, which he said is causing deep economic pain.
key_facts.excerpt: "We need to move beyond the 'no war, no peace' stalemate, which is causing deep economic pain for our countries," he said in Paris.

stories.headline: At least 11 NSA and Cyber Command workers died by suicide in a year, drawing White House and Congress scrutiny

key_facts.fact: At least 11 National Security Agency and US Cyber Command workers died by suicide over the 12 months ending in September, according to US officials and public records cited by Bloomberg, more than previously known.
key_facts.excerpt: At least 11 National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command workers died by suicide over roughly the past year, according to U.S. officials and public records, a greater number than previously known.

key_facts.fact: Ten of the deaths occurred around Fort Meade and one near an NSA facility in Georgia; they included military personnel, civilians and contractors.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the 12 months ending in September, 10 people working for the NSA or Cyber Command died by suicide around Fort Meade and one did near an NSA facility in Georgia, an official said... included military personnel, civilians and contractors

key_facts.fact: Five deaths between early June and early July were linked by the military as a suicide cluster; the most recent were a 21-year-old Army soldier and a 59-year-old NSA civilian in September.
key_facts.excerpt: The most recent suicides came after that in September, when a 21-year-old Army soldier and a 59-year-old civilian working for the NSA took their own lives

key_facts.fact: Officials say workloads surged in the past year because of foreign conflicts; Gen. Joshua Rudd requested $11 million in April for cyber personnel mental health, warning of 'burnout and force degradation'.
key_facts.excerpt: General Joshua Rudd, who became the leader of Cyber Command and the NSA in March, requested $11 million in April to address cyber personnel's mental health, warning of possible "burnout and force degradation."

key_facts.fact: Rudd mandated eight hours of uninterrupted rest in every 24-hour period and a 12-consecutive-hour work cap without a waiver.
key_facts.excerpt: Cyber personnel are broadly required to receive eight uninterrupted hours of rest in every 24-hour period and cannot work more than 12 consecutive hours without a waiver

stories.headline: FDA approves Merck KGaA's Pimjetmi pill for rare joint tumor TGCT

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 10, 2026, the FDA approved pimicotinib (Pimjetmi, EMD Serono), a kinase inhibitor, for adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) where surgery may cause worsening functional limitation or severe morbidity.
key_facts.excerpt: On November 10, 2026, the Food and Drug Administration approved pimicotinib (Pimjetmi, EMD Serono, Inc.), a kinase inhibitor, for adults with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT)

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 MANEUVER trial, the overall response rate at week 25 was 56% with pimicotinib versus 3.2% with placebo; 77% of responders had a response lasting at least 12 months.
key_facts.excerpt: ORR was 56% (95% CI: 42, 68) in the pimicotinib arm and 3.2% (95% CI: 0.1, 17) in the placebo arm... 27 (77%) had a DOR ≥12 months.

key_facts.fact: Pimjetmi is a once-daily oral CSF-1R inhibitor taken at 50 mg; EMD Serono is the US and Canada healthcare business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.
key_facts.excerpt: EMD Serono, the Healthcare business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany, in the US and Canada, announced today that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved PIMJETMI (pimicotinib), a once-daily oral colony stimulating factor-1 receptor (CSF-1R) inhibitor

key_facts.fact: TGCT is a rare, non-cancerous but locally aggressive tumor that grows in or around the lining of the joints; the FDA decision follows approvals in China, Canada and Switzerland.
key_facts.excerpt: TGCT, a rare and non-cancerous, locally aggressive tumor that grows in or around the lining of the joints... follows similar approvals from regulators in China, Canada and Switzerland.

key_facts.fact: The trial also showed significant gains in range of motion, physical functioning and pain versus placebo.
key_facts.excerpt: improving relative range of motion (p=0.0003), physical functioning (p=0.0074), and pain (p<0.0001).

stories.headline: Japan's Synspective books up to 10 Firefly Alpha launches for 20 radar satellites through 2030

key_facts.fact: Firefly Aerospace announced on Nov. 10 a multi-launch agreement with Japanese SAR satellite provider Synspective for up to 10 launches on its Alpha rocket through 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Firefly Aerospace (Nasdaq: FLY)... today announced a multi-launch agreement with Synspective Inc., a Japanese synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite data and solutions provider, for up to 10 launches on Firefly's Alpha rocket through 2030.

key_facts.fact: Each Alpha mission, with 1,000 kg lift capacity to low Earth orbit, will carry two StriX satellites, for up to 20 satellites in total.
key_facts.excerpt: With the ability to launch 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit, Alpha will deliver two of Synspective's SAR satellites to orbit per mission, deploying up to 20 total satellites.

key_facts.fact: Launches will fly from Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia and Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.
key_facts.excerpt: Firefly will launch Synspective's satellites from both Pad-0A at Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia and Space Launch Complex 2 at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California.

key_facts.fact: Synspective is also a major Rocket Lab customer and signed the largest commercial Electron contract last month, for 20 launches.
key_facts.excerpt: Synspective is also a major customer of Rocket Lab and signed the largest commercial contract for Electron last month for 20 launches, in addition to two previous 10-launch deals.

key_facts.fact: Firefly has not set a date for the next Alpha launch, the first in full Block II configuration, which it targets for the fourth quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Firefly hasn't set a specific date for the next launch of its Alpha rocket, which will feature the full Block II configuration for the first time... flight is targeted for the fourth quarter of this year.
